message.reasoning:
We need to see the conversation: user says "no SSO button, was I set up?" They ask why no SSO button appears. The policy excerpts include relevant info: DOC-010 part 1: "The SSO sign-in option only appears for an email domain the workspace has configured for SSO, and only once the identity provider sync has actually created that person's account." Also part 3: admin can check if account exists in Settings → People; absence means sync hasn't created it yet.

Thus we can answer: The SSO button only shows if your domain is configured and the sync created your account. If not, ask admin to verify account exists in Settings → People; if missing, sync hasn't run yet. Also enabling SSO doesn't disable password sign-in yet.

Provide answer accordingly. No need to escalate. Provide short answer.

function.arguments: {"message":"The SSO sign‑in button only appears for users whose email domain is configured for SSO **and** whose account has already been created by the identity‑provider sync. If you don’t see the button, it usually means the sync hasn’t provisioned your account yet. An admin can confirm whether your account exists by going to **Settings → People** – SSO‑provisioned accounts are marked with the identity provider name. If it’s missing, the sync needs to run or your domain may not be set up for SSO yet."}

arguments.message: The SSO sign‑in button only appears for users whose email domain is configured for SSO **and** whose account has already been created by the identity‑provider sync. If you don’t see the button, it usually means the sync hasn’t provisioned your account yet. An admin can confirm whether your account exists by going to **Settings → People** – SSO‑provisioned accounts are marked with the identity provider name. If it’s missing, the sync needs to run or your domain may not be set up for SSO yet.
